summary: Hosted chat streaming intermittently stalls (no new tokens) for VantaHealth
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports SSE stream starts, then stops emitting tokens after ~10-30s; client waits until their 60s idle timeout and aborts.

Impact: 3-8% of chat requests affected; end users see spinner/hang.

Environment: Hosted API, chat.completions streaming=true, region us-east.

Steps to reproduce (customer): send long prompt (~8k tokens) + tool call schema; observe occasional 'no chunks' after initial delta.

Notes: Customer sees HTTP connection still open; no chunks delivered. They are using Node fetch + EventSource-like parser.

Requested: root cause + mitigation; confirmation whether they should lower max_tokens or change timeout.
comments: Chloe Martin (Support): Seeing elevated p95 time-to-first-token? Customer says first token arrives quickly, then stalls mid-stream.

Ethan Park (Runtime): Pulled trace samples. Looks like generator continues but gateway isn't flushing chunks when upstream backpressure triggers. Hypothesis: nginx buffering path for chunked responses under certain headers.
Avery Johnson (SRE): Found that requests with 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' sometimes go through a path that enables proxy buffering. Proposed mitigation: force 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' on streaming routes.
Ethan Park: Patched gateway config in us-east canary. Stalls disappear in canary synthetic tests (perf-canary stream_hang check).
Chloe Martin: Customer confirms improvement after 2025-11-05 21:00 UTC; no hangs in last 24h.
Resolution: Gateway config change to disable buffering on SSE + ensure periodic flush; rollout complete in us-east. Follow-up task filed to add regression test for gzip + streaming.
